title: GTA started as a game where you played the cop
formula: GTA named in the first 2 s (the first GTA started with you playing the cop) -> strange act (your own police cars try to kill you) -> why (a bug, about to change games) -> the engine story (Mike adds a floor: top-down) -> the plan (Race'n'Chase, you're the cop, 18 months) -> problems (boring, crashes, the publisher asks every week to cancel it) -> tension (months run over) -> the bug (cops ram you; testers love being chased) -> the flip (you're the robber; peak) -> doubter paid off (the publisher stops asking) -> kicker (new name, the press outrage, 400 million) -> loop (the cops still try to kill you)
loop: Lines 1-2: the first GTA started with you playing the cop, and your own police cars keep trying to kill you. Last: and the cops? They still try to kill you, over the same pile-up shot.
facts: True history: every claim is in sources.md. The police-AI bug is a widely told legend (not confirmed by the developers in any interview we could read), so the narration says 'as the legend goes'.

'You' is an unnamed tester/developer at DMA Design in Dundee (a viewpoint, not a real person); Mike = Mike Dailly, Dave = David Jones (real, public, facts only; Mike's 'add a floor' idea is from his own account).
No game logos, screenshots or characters: the game is drawn in our own style (a top-down toy city).

lines.narration: The first GTA started with you playing the *cop*.
lines.spoken: The first G-T-A started with you playing the cop.
lines.scene: Cold open on a top-down toy city at night, our own style: a getaway car tears round a corner with a pack of police cars behind it, and big painted letters GTA? hang over the street. Hard cut at ~1 s: the same city in 1995 on a chunky office monitor, and the car being chased is a police car: yours. Face: confused.
lines.camera: Crane down onto the chase, hard cut to the monitor
lines.gag: The car being chased is a police car

lines.narration: And your own police cars keep trying to *kill* you.
lines.scene: You at the monitor in a cramped 1990s office: four police cars ram your little police car from every side. Face: shocked.
lines.camera: Push in over your shoulder onto the monitor
lines.gag: The police cars pile onto yours like a rugby scrum

lines.narration: It's a bug, and it's about to turn your cop game into Grand Theft *Auto*.
lines.scene: Freeze on the pile-up; a big red BUG stamp slams onto the screen. You lean back, grinning.
lines.camera: Hold on the frozen screen, pull back to your face
lines.gag: A BUG stamp slams onto the monitor

lines.narration: A year earlier, your coworker Mike has a game engine that only sees the *side* of things.
lines.scene: Flashback card 1994: Mike at his desk; on his monitor a side-on row of little buildings, like a stage set.
lines.camera: Slow push past Mike's shoulder
lines.gag: The buildings are flat cut-outs, like a puppet show

lines.narration: Then it hits him: all he needs is to add a *floor*.
lines.scene: Mike slides one floor tile under the side-on buildings; the whole city tips over backwards like a domino and lands flat.
lines.camera: Side view, the camera tips with the city
lines.gag: The whole city tips over and lands flat

lines.narration: Suddenly, you're looking straight *down* on a city.
lines.scene: The camera rises straight up: a top-down city of tiny roofs and roads; little cars start moving.
lines.camera: Crane straight up into the top-down view
lines.gag: Tiny cars start zooming around the roofs

lines.narration: Your boss Dave, the man behind *Lemmings*, builds a game on it.
lines.scene: Dave leans in, glasses flashing; he slaps a sticky note on Mike's monitor: NEW GAME.
lines.camera: Two-shot, quick push
lines.gag: Dave slaps a sticky note on the monitor

lines.narration: It's called Race'n'Chase. You're the cop, you chase robbers, done in *18* months.
lines.spoken: It's called Race-and-Chase. You're the cop, you chase robbers, done in eighteen months.
lines.scene: A whiteboard: stick-figure cop chasing a stick-figure robber, a wall calendar with 18 months circled.
lines.camera: Pan across the whiteboard to the calendar
lines.gag: The calendar has 18 months circled in red

lines.narration: There's just one problem. Being the cop is *boring*.
lines.scene: You as a cop car in the game, politely following a robber car at walking pace; both drivers yawn.
lines.camera: Top-down game view, then your yawning face
lines.gag: The cop and the robber yawn at the same time

lines.narration: And the game crashes. Constantly. The cars handle like *shopping carts*.
lines.scene: The monitor freezes into a mess of pixels; in the game, a police car spins out like a runaway shopping cart.
lines.camera: Hard cuts: frozen screen, spinning car
lines.gag: A police car wobbles like a runaway shopping cart

lines.narration: Every week, the publisher asks one question: can we *cancel* it?
lines.scene: A man in a suit opens the office door, holding a giant rubber CANCEL stamp; the calendar flips a page; he opens the door again, and again.
lines.camera: Locked on the door, calendar flipping between
lines.gag: The publisher's CANCEL stamp gets bigger every week

lines.narration: Month 18 comes and goes. Then month 20. Then month *24*.
lines.spoken: Month eighteen comes and goes. Then month twenty. Then month twenty-four.
lines.scene: Calendar pages tear off and fly past your head; the coffee cups on your desk pile up into a tower.
lines.camera: Fast push on the calendar
lines.gag: Your coffee cups stack into a tower

lines.narration: Then, as the legend goes, the police *break*.
lines.scene: Close on the monitor: the police cars' little headlights flick to red, all at once.
lines.camera: Snap in on the screen
lines.gag: The cop cars' headlights turn red

lines.narration: The cop cars stop pulling you over. They ram you off the *road*.
lines.scene: Top-down game: the police cars swerve straight at your car and ram it into a wall.
lines.camera: Top-down chase, shaking on each hit
lines.gag: The cops ram you into a wall

lines.narration: Testers skip the missions. They just let the cops *chase* them.
lines.scene: A crowd of testers around one monitor, cheering and laughing as a police pack chases a little car round and round.
lines.camera: Wide on the cheering crowd
lines.gag: Testers cheer like it's a football match

lines.narration: So the team asks: if running is the fun part, why are we the *police*?
lines.scene: Everyone turns to the whiteboard; Dave rubs out the stick-figure cop's hat.
lines.camera: Push in on the whiteboard
lines.gag: Dave rubs out the cop's hat

lines.narration: You flip it. You're not the cop anymore. You're the *robber*.
lines.scene: In the game, your little car's police lights pop off and roll away; you, at the desk, swap a police cap for a striped robber's beanie.
lines.camera: Hard cut from the game to your cap swap
lines.gag: Your police lights fall off and roll away

lines.narration: Steal any car, and every cop in town comes after *you*.
lines.scene: Top-down city: your car steals away and a river of police cars pours after it down every street.
lines.camera: Crane up as the police pour after you
lines.gag: A river of police cars floods the streets

lines.narration: And the publisher? It finally stops asking to *cancel* it.
lines.scene: The man in the suit lowers his giant CANCEL stamp and quietly stamps a coffee cup instead.
lines.camera: Two-shot, slow push
lines.gag: He stamps a coffee cup instead

lines.narration: Race'n'Chase gets a new name: Grand Theft *Auto*.
lines.spoken: Race-and-Chase gets a new name: Grand Theft Auto.
lines.scene: A game box, our own painted design: a top-down city and a getaway car; the name painted across it.
lines.camera: Spin the box to the lens
lines.gag: The box spins into frame

lines.narration: Before it's even out, newspapers call it a game for thugs, and Parliament debates *banning* it.
lines.scene: A newspaper slams down with a screaming headline; cut to rows of old lords in robes, shaking their fists.
lines.camera: Newspaper insert, whip to the lords
lines.gag: The lords shake their fists in unison
lines.spoken: Before it's even out, newspapers call it a game for thugs, and Parliament debates banning it.

lines.narration: Best free advert a game ever *had*.
lines.scene: Outside a shop, a queue of players stretches round the block.
lines.camera: Wide on the queue
lines.gag: The queue wraps around the whole block

lines.narration: Today, the series has sold over 400 million *copies*.
lines.spoken: Today, the series has sold over four-hundred million copies.
lines.scene: A sales counter rolls past 100, 200, 300, 400 million; the digits smoke.
lines.camera: Push in on the counter
lines.gag: The sales counter smokes

lines.narration: And the cops? They still try to *kill* you.
lines.scene: Back at the 1995 monitor: police cars ram your little car; you grin.
lines.camera: Same framing as line 1
lines.gag: The same pile-up as the first shot
